_comment: Scopes Pylance/pyright to FIRST-PARTY code. Two reasons, and the second matters more than the warning that
prompted this.
(1) Volume. The workspace holds ~250 first-party .py files and 13,116 under .venv, so the editor was
indexing site-packages as if it were project source. That is the 'large number of source files'
advisory: a performance complaint, not a correctness one.
(2) DUPLICATE MODULE TREES, which is the real hazard. This repo deliberately keeps several copies of the
wcEcoli package layout — model_overlay/cleaned/models/ecoli/..., vendor/v301/models/ecoli/...,
archive/, and loose scripts under runs/. With those indexed, auto-import happily offers
'from models.ecoli.processes.polypeptide_elongation import ...' resolved against the ARCHIVED copy, and
the editor reports no error. In a repo whose whole subject is knowing which artefact a number came
from, an IDE silently binding a symbol to the wrong copy of a module is the same defect class in a new
place.
venvPath/venv are set rather than just excluding .venv: excluding it would stop imports resolving at all.
This keeps it as the ENVIRONMENT while removing it from the indexed workspace.
TYPE CHECKING IS OFF, DELIBERATELY, and the first version of this file got that wrong.
It set typeCheckingMode 'basic', which switched type checking ON across a codebase that has never
been annotated for it. The result was squiggles in ~20 files at once — and every one I read was
correct, working code that a checker cannot prove: a Vega-Lite spec dict inferred as dict[str,str]
then given a nested dict (tools.py:703/706/777), and inspect.signature() on a Callable|None whose
None case is already caught by the except clause two lines down (tools.py:1541). None of them is a
bug; 1082 tests pass and CI is green.
Scoping the indexer and turning on a type checker are different decisions, and only the first was
asked for. ruff is this project's linter and runs in CI. Anyone who wants type checking can set this
to 'basic' or 'standard' — that is a deliberate choice with real cleanup behind it, not a default.
NOT VERIFIED against pyright itself — no pyright binary is installed here (no PATH entry, no npx cache).
The shape follows the documented schema; the check that matters is that imports still resolve in the
editor (see .vscode/settings.json for what each file is responsible for).
